ROLE OF THE TREASURER’S OFFICE
The County Treasurer’s Office, established by the Michigan State Constitution, has duties defined by state law and the County Board of Commissioners. The Treasurer is also part of the Plat Board, Elections Commission, County Apportionment Commission, and Land Bank Authority.
Main Responsibilities
Managing County Funds: The Treasurer receives, safeguards, and invests county funds, prioritizing safety and return on investment, with a preference for local investments.
Collecting Delinquent Taxes: Each March 1, unpaid property taxes are turned over to the County Treasurer. The office then collects these taxes, including interest and penalties, and handles foreclosures on unpaid properties.
Additional Duties
Dog Licenses: Issuance of three-year dog licenses, expiring with the rabies vaccination month, to spread renewals throughout the year and save costs.
PRE Audit: Conducts annual audits of Primary Residence Exemptions (PRE) to ensure compliance, improving efficiency and reducing property owner frustration.
Certifying Deeds: Ensures all delinquent taxes are paid for recorded warranty deeds. The office has transitioned to electronic certification, improving efficiency and reducing costs.
DOG LICENSE PRICE SCHEDULE
After many requests from dog owners, we recently switched to a three-year license system. The licenses expire at the end of the month the rabies vaccination expires, instead of all licenses expiring at the end of the year. By doing this, we spread the renewals throughout the year rather than having everyone renewing in the same few months. This also requires only about a third of dog owners to renew each year.
License Rates
Three-year licenses: $30.00 for sterile dogs or $60.00 for non-sterile dogs.
Two-year licenses: $20.00 for sterile dogs or $40.00 for non-sterile dogs.
One-year licenses: $10.00 for sterile dogs or $20.00 for non-sterile dogs.
* Owners need to present proof of rabies vaccination when purchasing a dog license.
Kennel Licenses
Less than 10 dogs: $55
10 to 20 dogs: $75
* Kennel owners need to present approval papers from Animal Control when purchasing kennel licenses.

PROPERTY TAX CYCLE
In October 1999, the Legislature enacted significant changes to the State’s tax-reversion process. Public Act 123 establishes a new tax-reversion process in which annual tax lien sales were eliminated in favor of an annual forfeiture and judicial foreclosure process.
Your County Treasurer is responsible for the foreclosure and sale of tax-reverted property. By having your Treasurer handle the process, the County of Emmet has local control over the entire tax-reversion process from beginning to end. The ENTIRE PROCESS takes place locally, allowing the County of Emmet – NOT LANSING – to create solutions to meet particular taxpayer needs.
FOUR MAJOR STEPS UNDER THIS SYSTEM
Delinquency
Taxes billed by your city, village, or township treasurer and not paid by the taxpayer will be returned delinquent to the County Treasurer on March 1st as required by Michigan law. A 4% Administration fee and interest of 1% per month will be added beginning March 1st, and a $15.00 mailing fee on October 1st. The following March 1st, the property will be placed in
Forfeiture
Interest and fees will increase. When a property is forfeited, the law requires that the interest rate go from 1% per month to 1.5% per month retroactive to the date the taxes became delinquent. IN ADDITION, FEES (a minimum of $248.00) MUST BE ADDED. On December 1st, a $50.00 publication fee must be added. After a property has been in forfeiture for ONE YEAR, on April 1st, it will be placed in
Forclosure
At this point, title work will have taken place. Mailing and publishing of notices will have also taken place, as well as Administrative Show Cause Hearings and Judicial Foreclosure Hearings. See our documents section above for the Hearing Notice. Once the above process has been completed, the Circuit Court enters a judgment of foreclosure quieting title, and if the taxes are not redeemed by March 31st, the County Treasurer assumes ownership and starts the process of
Land Disposition
THIS IS THE SALE OF THE PROPERTY. The former owner cannot get the property back after it has been foreclosed. Foreclosure is final! Property that has been foreclosed will be sold at Public Auction to the highest bidder. ALL SALES WILL BE FINAL WITH NO RECOURSE BY THE PREVIOUS LANDOWNER TO RECLAIM TITLE TO THE PROPERTY. For further information on these land sales, check www.tax-sale.info .
It is extremely important to understand this law that took effect on October 1, 1999. For a property tax timeline, click here .
PROPERTY TAX TIMELINE
First Year
Taxes are billed and collected by the local unit. Summer tax bills are mailed by July 1, and Winter tax bills are mailed by December 1.
Second Year
On March 1, unpaid taxes become delinquent and payable to the County Treasurer. A statutory 4% administration fee and 1% interest per month are added. On October 1, a $15.00 mail fee is added.
Third Year
On March 1, the property is forfeited to the County Treasurer. Per Michigan law, the interest increases to 1.5% per month and is retroactive back to the date the taxes first became delinquent, and additional fees of at least $248.00 are added. On June 1, title research begins, personal visits are made to each property, and properties are posted. On December 1, a $50.00 statutory publication fee is added to all parcels that remain delinquent. During December, properties and all names with a legal interest are published in the newspaper.
Final Redemption Period
In January and/or February, a show cause hearing is held by the County Treasurer, and a Circuit Court Foreclosure Hearing is conducted. See our documents section above for the Hearing Notice. March 31 is the last day to redeem property. All redemption rights expire on April 1. At Foreclosure, all persons with any interest lose all rights. Title to property passes to the County Treasurer. In August, the property is sold at public auction. For information, visit www.tax-sale.info .

PRINCIPAL RESIDENCE EXEMPTION
A Principal Residence Exemption (PRE) exempts a residence from up to 18 mills of local school district tax for school operating purposes. To qualify, you must be a Michigan resident who owns and occupies the property as a principal residence. The PRE is separate from the Homestead Property Tax Credit.
Our office conducts the PRE Audit locally, identifying and verifying properties claiming the PRE. We send letters to property owners to clarify discrepancies. If owners do not respond, we are required to deny the exemption and bill the parcels with 1.25% interest per month from the original delinquency date. The collected interest is shared between the local unit, the State, and the County, with most remaining in Emmet County.

GENERAL FAQ
What services does the Emmet County Treasurer's Office provide?
The Emmet County Treasurer's Office handles property tax collection, management of county funds, disbursement of tax revenues, and other financial services for the county.
Can I pay my taxes online?
Yes, you can pay your taxes online through our secure payment portal. Visit our website and click on the “Pay Online” link in Department Resources .
What forms of payment are accepted for tax payments?
We accept checks, money orders, and electronic payments. Credit card payments can be made online, but a convenience fee may apply.
How do I apply for a tax payment plan?
You can apply for a tax payment plan by contacting our office. We will provide you with the necessary forms and information on eligibility.
What should I do if I cannot pay my taxes on time?
If you cannot pay your taxes on time, contact our office as soon as possible to discuss your options, including possible payment plans and assistance programs.
How do I obtain a duplicate tax bill?
You can request a duplicate tax bill by contacting our office via phone, email, or in person. There may be a small fee for this service.
What is the procedure for a property tax refund?
If you are eligible for a property tax refund, you will need to submit a refund request form along with any supporting documentation. Our office will process the request and issue a refund if approved.
